nodes.label: 5-Step ESD Decision Logic
nodes.rationale: Step 1 trusts vendor RO ESD directly (no AI) because the vendor promise date is more authoritative than free-text notes. AI is only called when RO ESD is blank. Offsets are applied deterministically in code, never in the prompt, to keep the model from drift-affecting the offset logic. Stale past dates are overridden to no_esd_found rather than surfaced.

nodes.label: Swappable ESD Inference Provider Architecture
nodes.rationale: EsdInferenceProvider interface in types.ts makes the AI model/vendor swappable. AzureOpenAiEsdProvider is a deliberate stub seam for future use. DryRunEsdProvider enables full pipeline testing with zero API calls, which is critical when no API key is available.

nodes.label: MXI Write Safety - Human Approval Only
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable principle: the writer never runs automatically. Only executes when explicitly approved, one order at a time. No code path exists from inference-computed to MXI-updated without a human approval action. MXI_ENV defaults to stage, never production. Every approve/reject call produces exactly one mxi_writes audit row.
nodes.norm_label: mxi write safety - human approval only

nodes.label: DOM .fill() vs Keypress for Masked Date Input Fields
nodes.source_location: Write path addendum - corruption bug section
nodes.rationale: Older masked/validated date inputs enforce per-keystroke JS validation that rejects further input once 'full', regardless of selection state. Using .fill() sets the value via DOM input/change event directly, bypassing per-keystroke validation. Click+Backspace+type approach silently corrupted live data twice before this was discovered.
nodes.norm_label: dom .fill() vs keypress for masked date input fields

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Trail Pattern
nodes.rationale: Both esd_inferences and mxi_writes tables are append-only - rows are never updated or deleted. This creates a full audit trail for answering 'why did this date change' and enables diffing results across runs.

nodes.label: git check-ignore -v for Gitignore Validation
nodes.rationale: A gitignore entry that visually looks right still needs git check-ignore -v to confirm it actually matches. The .env and discovery-recording.ts entries had literal quote characters wrapping them, meaning the real secrets-holding .env file was not being ignored despite appearing to be in a visual read.

nodes.label: Order Orphan Rate - Reporting Coverage Not a Bug
nodes.rationale: 387 CRA-only orphans reflect reporting coverage (Vendor OOR is only current week replies from a subset of vendors; CRA OOR is all open orders). Vendor-name overlap alone is not a meaningful bug signal. The real diagnostic is exact Part Number + Serial Number match under a different Order Number for the same vendor - zero such duplicates found.
nodes.norm_label: order orphan rate - reporting coverage not a bug

nodes.label: MXI Session Management - Login-Once, Retry-Once-Then-Halt
nodes.rationale: Login/session loss is categorically different from a per-order data problem. A failed login at startup does not crash the server - it logs loudly and puts the client in a failed state. GET /health, GET /pending-esd-updates, and POST /reject still work without MXI, while POST /approve fails immediately with a clear error recorded as an audit row.

nodes.label: Write Reporting Failure vs Record Being Wrong Are Different Facts
nodes.rationale: writeEsd's read-back check correctly caught mismatches and reported failure, but the corrupted value had already been submitted to the live stage record. A write reporting failure and a record being left in a wrong state are two different facts - checking only the former misses corrupted live data.
nodes.norm_label: write reporting failure vs record being wrong are different facts
